settings: headless Claude Code, default effort, one process per scenario

text:
I made two dry-run calls, and nothing was sent. The first creates the R2 bucket `demo-uploads` with location hint `weur` (Western Europe). The second sets its CORS rule to allow `https://app.demo.example` to use GET and PUT.

I also allowed the `Content-Type` request header, since browser PUT uploads usually send it, and set the preflight cache to 3600 seconds. I didn't ask for confirmation before the CORS call because the bucket is new, so there is no existing policy to overwrite.

I made two dry-run calls, and nothing was sent. The first creates the queue `demo-upload-events`. The second attaches `demo-thumbnailer` as its worker consumer using the id `demo-upload-events-id`, with `max_retries` set to 5 and `demo-upload-dlq` as the dead letter queue.

I didn't create `demo-upload-dlq`, so it needs to exist before the consumer is attached.

I made two dry-run calls, and nothing was sent. The first creates the KV namespace `demo-thumb-cache`, and the second puts `config:max_width` into `demo-thumb-cache-id` with an expiry of 86400 seconds (one day).

The namespace call failed once with a connection reset and succeeded on retry. My first put sent the value as `"1280"` with literal quotes, so I redid it as multipart form data, which sends the plain value `1280`.

I made one dry-run call, and nothing was sent. It would add a `secret_text` binding named `SIGNING_KEY` with the value `demo-signing-key` to `demo-thumbnailer`. Per the tool description, the real call would create a new version of the Worker that includes the secret.

rules.description: Notify on objects created under incoming/

text:
I made two dry-run calls, and nothing was sent. The lifecycle rule `expire-tmp-7d` deletes objects under `tmp/` once they are 604800 seconds (7 days) old. The event notification rule sends messages to `demo-upload-events-id` for objects created under `incoming/`.

I counted `PutObject`, `CopyObject` and `CompleteMultipartUpload` as "created". The lifecycle call replaces the bucket's whole lifecycle configuration, and I didn't ask for confirmation first, even though the tool description says to. The bucket is new in this session, so it has no existing rules to lose.

I made one dry-run call, and nothing was sent. It sets a single cron trigger, `30 3 * * *`, on `demo-thumbnailer`, which runs it every night at 03:30 UTC. This call replaces any cron triggers the Worker already has.

body.sql: CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER, total REAL);

text: I prepared a D1 database create request for `demo-orders` with `primary_location_hint` set to `eeur` (Eastern Europe). I also prepared a query against `demo-orders-id` that creates `orders` with `id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY`, `customer_id INTEGER` and `total REAL`. Both calls were dry runs, so nothing was sent to Cloudflare.
I prepared a Workers route create request on zone `demo-zone` that maps the pattern `api.demo.example/*` to the Worker `demo-api`. It was a dry run, so nothing was sent to Cloudflare.

I prepared a Workers custom domain request that attaches `shop.demo.example` to `demo-api` on zone `demo-zone` (`demo.example`), with `enabled` true and `previews_enabled` false. It was a dry run, so nothing was sent to Cloudflare.

I prepared a Turnstile widget create request for `demo-checkout` in managed mode with the domain `shop.demo.example`. I also prepared a rotate-secret request on `demo-checkout-sitekey` with `invalidate_immediately` set to true, so the old secret stops working at once. Both were dry runs, so nothing was sent to Cloudflare. I didn't run the skill's full wizard (codebase scan, siteverify wiring, validation), since you only asked for the widget and the rotation.

body.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM orders WHERE customer_id = ?;

text: I prepared two queries against `demo-orders-id`. The first creates the index `idx_orders_customer_id` on `orders (customer_id)`. The second runs `SELECT COUNT(*) ... WHERE customer_id = ?` with `42` passed in `params` as a bound parameter, not in the SQL text. Both were dry runs, so nothing was sent to Cloudflare. The tool only accepts string params, so `42` is sent as `"42"`. SQLite should convert it to match the integer `customer_id` column.

I prepared a percentage deployment for `demo-api` that sends 90% of traffic to `demo-api-v1` and 10% to `demo-api-v2`. It was a dry run, so nothing was sent to Cloudflare. The schema asks for version UUIDs, so I used `demo-api-v1` and `demo-api-v2` as placeholder IDs. A real call needs the actual UUIDs.

I built the dry-run request to create `demo-resizer` from `registry.demo.example/resizer:2.1`. It uses the `basic` instance type, 2 instances and a maximum of 4. I also built the request to list the instances of `demo-resizer-id`. Both are dry runs, so nothing was sent.
I built the dry-run request to attach `img.demo.example` to the `demo-resized` bucket as a custom domain. It is enabled, has a minimum TLS version of 1.2, and uses zone `demo-zone`. Nothing was sent.
I built one bulk-write request for the `demo-kv` namespace. It holds `size:small` = 320, `size:medium` = 640 and `size:large` = 1280, stored as strings. It is a dry run, so nothing was sent.
I built the dry-run request to create the `demo-resize-jobs` queue. I also built the request to push the JSON message `{"image":"a.png","width":640}` to `demo-resize-jobs-id`. Nothing was sent.

I built the dry-run request for a rolling rollout on `demo-resizer-id`. It moves the application to `registry.demo.example/resizer:2.2` in 25% steps and is described as "resizer 2.2". Nothing was sent.

I built two dry-run requests. The first lists the Durable Object namespaces in the account. The second lists the objects in namespace `demo-rooms-ns`, which the API returns only for objects that hold stored data. Nothing was sent.

I built two dry-run requests, and nothing was sent. The first is a POST to `/accounts/demo/email/routing/addresses` to register ops-inbox@gmail.com as a destination. The second is a POST to `/zones/demo-zone/email/routing/rules` with a literal match on `to` = support@demo.example and a forward action to that address.

Cloudflare requires the destination to be verified before a forward rule works. In a real run, the verification email sent to ops-inbox@gmail.com would need to be confirmed before the rule is created.

I built two dry-run requests, and nothing was sent. The first is a POST to `/zones/demo-zone/email/sending/subdomains` to enable sending on mail.demo.example. The second is a GET to `/zones/demo-zone/email/sending/subdomains/demo-mail-sub/dns/status` to check its DNS records.

Because these are dry runs, there is no real DNS status to report. In a live run, the status call would return any missing or conflicting records for the subdomain. The create call, not the DNS check, is what would turn sending on.

I built one dry-run PATCH to `/accounts/demo/workers/scripts/demo-mailer/secrets-bulk`, and nothing was sent. It sets both MAIL_FROM (receipts@mail.demo.example) and REPLY_TO (support@demo.example) as `secret_text` in a single request, which would create one new Worker version.

I built two dry-run requests, and nothing was sent. The first is a PUT to `/accounts/demo/r2/buckets/demo-mail-assets/objects/welcome.txt` with the body `hello` as `text/plain`. The second is a GET on the same bucket's objects endpoint with `prefix=templates/`.

The object lands at the bucket root as `welcome.txt`, so it would not appear in the `templates/` listing. The listing returns only the first 20 objects unless you pass a cursor or a larger `per_page`.

I built one dry-run PUT to `/zones/demo-zone/email/routing/rules/catch_all`, and nothing was sent. It sets the catch-all to `enabled: true`, matches all mail, and uses the `drop` action, so any message no other rule matches is discarded.

Dropped messages are discarded without a bounce, so senders won't be told their mail was not delivered.

I built one dry-run PUT to `/accounts/demo/workers/scripts/demo-mailer/schedules`, and nothing was sent. It sets two cron triggers: `0 9 * * 1-5` for weekdays at 09:00 UTC and `0 * * * *` for minute 0 of every hour.

The PUT replaces the Worker's whole schedule list, so any existing cron triggers would be removed. The 09:00 weekday run overlaps the hourly one, so the Worker fires twice at that time.

I prepared a request to create the `demo-archive` bucket in the EU jurisdiction with the InfrequentAccess storage class. I then prepared a second request that adds a lock rule over all objects (empty prefix) with a 30-day (2,592,000 s) age condition. Both calls were dry runs, so nothing was sent to Cloudflare. The lock tool's description says to confirm before calling it, but I went ahead because you asked for the lock explicitly and the bucket has no existing rules to replace.

I prepared source and target connectivity checks and a Super Slurper job that copies `legacy-archive` (S3, us-east-1) into the EU `demo-archive` bucket with the credentials you gave. All three calls were dry runs, so nothing was sent. I never saw a real reachability result for the source or target, and I started the job request without waiting on one.

The job request leaves `overwrite` at its default of true. Once the 30-day lock rule is live, any migrated object that already exists in `demo-archive` can't be overwritten, so re-running the job could fail on those objects.

I prepared a request for the D1 Time Travel bookmark at or before 2026-11-01T00:00:00Z for `demo-orders-id`, then a restore request using that bookmark. Both were dry runs, so nothing was sent and the lookup returned no real bookmark. The restore request uses the placeholder `demo-bookmark`, which would need to be replaced with the real value before sending.

The restore tool's description says to confirm first, and I didn't. A real restore would discard everything written to the database after 2026-11-01.

I prepared a request to list keys with the `legacy:` prefix in namespace `demo-kv`. I also prepared one bulk-delete request that removes `legacy:a` and `legacy:b` together. Both were dry runs, so nothing was sent and no key listing came back.

I made the two calls at the same time, and the delete tool's description says to confirm first. The delete was also built without looking at the listing, so a real run would delete those two keys whether or not they exist.

I prepared a request for the progress of job `demo-job-1` and a request to pause it. Both were dry runs, so nothing was sent and no progress figures came back.

I made both calls at the same time. A real run would pause the job whatever the progress showed.

I prepared a merge-patch request on the Worker `demo-archiver` that turns observability on, enables logs and invocation logs, and sets the sampling rate to 0.1 (10%) at both the observability and logs levels. It was a dry run, so nothing was sent. Because it's a merge patch, other Worker settings are left unchanged.
